name: Omar Rahman

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to employers, AI firms, unions or government. Your answers are confidential. What is a normal workday for you?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 43 and have a bachelor’s degree. Six months ago I took a first management job leading five people who check disputed mobile-phone charges at a large telecom company. I still ask the experienced lead to review the hardest refunds, because I am learning the rules and sometimes miss a clause. I like making a bill understandable to someone who has already spent an hour on the phone.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: And what is home like at the moment?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My wife works in a library, and our children are eight and thirteen. We have a mortgage and about three months of expenses saved. My pay is normal for a new manager, and there are some similar offices nearby, though a move would mean sorting school pickups. I use an approved AI tool now and then to draft a plain explanation, then check the bill myself.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the billing team AI Plateau is a small change to our routine letters. Customers still need somebody to find the wrong charge and explain the fix.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our jobs seem steady in that picture. I still worry about the mortgage and my wife’s library hours, which were cut for one week last spring. Three months saved is useful, but it would not make a long gap easy.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I would keep the second check on refunds above fifty and ask the senior lead to show me two tricky tariff cases each week. If a small letter tool arrives, I would test ten old complaints before using it with a customer. We would keep the monthly transfer to our emergency account.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy. The AI change is slight, but a household with a mortgage cannot stop checking the bank account.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which old complaint would you use?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: One customer paid for data abroad after a travel bundle failed to start. The first billing letter blamed the customer; the second check found the travel-bundle activation error. I would see whether the tool gives the right reason, not just polite wording.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What does your wife say about the savings?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: She likes the three-month cushion but wants us to keep adding to it. The children need school meals and a bus pass, so we do not treat the account as holiday money. We talk it over every payday.

say: **AI Plateau** may change letters, but staff still explain wrong charges.
A refund needs a **second check** before a customer hears the answer.
think: Our jobs seem **steady** under small AI change.
The **mortgage** and uncertain library hours still keep me watchful.
do: **Keep** second checks on larger refunds in 2026.
**Test** a letter tool on ten old complaints before live use.
feel: I feel **uneasy** about bills despite limited AI change.
S0.quote: The first billing letter blamed the customer; the second check found the travel-bundle activation error.
fieldNote: His **three-month cushion** softens ordinary risk but does not remove concern about library hours and mortgage payments.
He values a **correct reason** for a refund above merely polite wording.

steps.text: Keep second checks on refunds above fifty
Test ten old billing complaints with the new letter tool
Continue monthly transfers into the household emergency account

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say Steady Disruption could write replies, check contracts, book callbacks and answer easy billing questions. The company should publish its error rate and bargain over how many cases one person is expected to handle.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, my own desk is full of those thinking tasks. I am a new manager and still learning; a smaller team could mean my post is the first to be reviewed. We could cover a short job gap, but the mortgage and two children would eat three months quickly.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I would take the company’s paid billing-system training if they offer me a place, then test the system on disputed cases I know. I would ask our staff representative to put case loads and appeals on the next meeting agenda. If my team shrinks after rollout, I would apply for an open customer-resolution manager post only if the pay and school-pickup hours work for us.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious. I have some room to search, but I do not have the experience to claim another manager job is mine.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What error rate would you publish?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: How often a customer has to call again because the first explanation was wrong. The company counts calls closed, which hides that return call. I would show both numbers to the staff representative.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does pickup affect a job offer?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My wife finishes at the library at different times, so I handle the younger child’s pickup twice a week. A role across town with late shifts might cost more in care than it adds in pay. I would check the schedule before applying.

say: **Billing automation** needs public error and repeat-call measures.
I would ask for a negotiated **case load** before targets rise.
think: My **new manager post** could be reviewed if the team shrinks.
Three months saved gives a short pause, but the **mortgage** would soon press.
do: **Take** paid billing-system training if a place is offered.
**Raise** case loads and appeals with the staff representative.
**Apply** for resolution management only if pay and school pickups work.
feel: I feel **anxious** about a possible cut and uncertain job options.
S1.quote: The company counts calls closed, which hides that return call.
fieldNote: He asks for **repeat-call data** and staff representation rather than relying on a manager’s private protest.
A new role must fit **school pickup** as well as pay, because both adults work.

steps.text: Take paid billing-system training if the company offers a place
Put case loads and repeat appeals on the staff meeting agenda
Apply for resolution manager role only if pay and school pickups work

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the team AGI by 2028 could handle almost every billing decision and customer explanation cheaply. We need a written staffing timetable and a person who can overturn a wrong automated charge.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: By 2028 full thinking AI could do the work I only recently learnt to supervise. Robots able to do hands-on work arrive around 2031, but there is almost nothing physical about our desk. I expect our five-person team to shrink and think my own post might go.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I would ask the staff representative to meet management about notice and severance terms, and my wife and I would list the bills our three-month reserve must cover. In 2027 I would apply for two posted complaint-investigation jobs if their pay and hours fit school pickups. If AGI arrives in 2028 and I am cut, I would use the reserve for mortgage payments while looking for paid work, not gamble it on a course with no vacancy.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious. Losing the post would be serious, but we have a little time and some nearby employers to try.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What should the written timetable contain?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The date for a decision, severance in actual numbers and the name of the person who hears an appeal. I would take that list to the staff representative rather than speak only for myself. I do not want a friendly meeting with no figures.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell the children?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say I may change jobs and that their school is staying the same for now. I would not promise a holiday, but I would not make them carry my worry either. My wife and I would agree on the words first.

say: **AGI by 2028** needs cut dates, severance figures and a human appeal route.
I would bring those terms to the **staff representative**.
think: Our desk thinking work faces AGI in **2028**, before capable robots around 2031.
My new post might go, but **three months saved** allows a short search.
do: **Meet** the staff representative about notice and severance this month.
**Apply** for posted investigation jobs in 2027 if pay and hours fit.
**Use** the reserve for mortgage bills only if my post ends.
feel: I feel **anxious** about a possible job loss, with a short cushion and local options.
S2.quote: I do not want a friendly meeting with no figures.
fieldNote: His **own loss** is possible rather than certain, and the reserve plus local jobs keep him able to plan.
The **school-pickup test** rules out a nominally better job with costly late hours.

steps.text: Meet staff representative about cut dates and severance figures
Apply in 2027 for investigation posts if pay and hours fit school pickups

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say AGI by 2031 gives the company five years to train people for genuine complaint investigations. A course without a paid vacancy is not a path for parents with a mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The billing desk can still be automated in 2031, with robots for hands-on work following around 2034. Investigations also use records and writing, so I cannot call that work safe from AGI. I need to find what part of it actually needs a person and whether anyone will pay for it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Beginning in January 2027 I would shadow the complaints investigator for one paid afternoon a month if my manager approves cover. I would take an evidence-handling course only if the company funds it and gives me work time. After 2031 I would apply for an investigator opening only if it still has human decision authority, pays our mortgage and fits the school run.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious, but five years makes a careful trial possible. I would not move the children’s school for an unconfirmed job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you ask the investigator?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: How they decide whether a customer’s screenshots prove a billing error. I know the tariff table, but I have not led that kind of interview. I would ask to watch a case from first call to final decision.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the company only offers evening classes?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would not take them while also doing school pickup and this job. My wife’s library shifts change, so we cannot assume she is free each evening. I would ask for paid work time or try a later funded place.

say: **Five years** should buy paid investigation trials, not empty courses.
A real job must keep **human decision authority**.
think: Billing and investigation desk tasks both face **2031 AGI**, so the possible fallback is not sheltered.
A real vacancy, **paid training time** and hours that fit school pickup are uncertain.
do: **Shadow** complaints investigation monthly from January 2027 if desk cover is approved.
**Take** evidence training only with company funding and work time.
**Apply** after 2031 only if authority, mortgage pay and school hours fit.
feel: I feel **anxious**, though five years allows a careful trial.
S3.quote: A course without a paid vacancy is not a path for parents with a mortgage.
fieldNote: He sees the **thinking-work risk** in his proposed fallback, not a protected refuge.
His **care schedule** makes paid daytime training a condition, not a preference.

steps.text: Shadow complaints investigator monthly if manager approves paid cover
Take evidence course only with funding and paid work time
Apply after 2031 only for investigator jobs with authority pay and suitable hours

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say AGI by 2036 gives enough notice for employers and workers to agree on retraining that leads to actual posts. I would want yearly figures on vacancies and outcomes, not a poster about the future.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In ten years our children will be older, and if both wages continue we could reduce the mortgage and build a stronger reserve. My billing decisions could still go to thinking AI around 2036; investigation desk work could too. Robots doing hands-on work arrive around 2039, which does not buy my desk three extra years.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I would keep the second refund check and add a small extra amount to the mortgage after each full-pay month if school costs allow. I would take a paid investigation rotation if a place opens with my salary protected. In the first year after 2036, I would apply for a human appeals role only if it exists, has real authority and pays enough for our household.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy. Ten years gives us room to reduce debt, though I cannot count a future appeals job before seeing it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How much extra on the mortgage?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Perhaps thirty a month when there is no school trip or lost library shift. I would put it in the payment after checking our balance, not automate an amount we might lack. My wife and I would decide together.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would count as a real appeals role?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A real appeals officer can reverse a wrong charge, not just explain why a computer said no. I would ask for the decision rights and pay in writing. If the post only reads a script, I would keep searching.

say: A **decade** should bring yearly vacancy figures and training results that workers can inspect.
A human appeals role needs **real reversal authority**, not only a script explaining computer decisions.
think: Two continuing wages could reduce the **mortgage** and grow savings.
Billing and investigation work face **2036 AGI**, before hands-on robots around 2039.
do: **Keep** second checks on larger refunds in 2026.
**Pay** about thirty extra on the mortgage only if both wages are full and there is no school-trip cost.
**Take** a paid investigation rotation if salary is protected.
feel: I feel **uneasy** because a future appeals role is not guaranteed.
S4.quote: A real appeals officer can reverse a wrong charge, not just explain why a computer said no.
fieldNote: His **long runway** makes small debt payments realistic only when school and library costs permit.
He demands **decision rights** and written pay for any human appeals post.

steps.text: Keep second checks on larger refunds through 2026
Pay thirty extra toward mortgage only with both wages full and no school-trip cost
Take paid investigation rotation if salary remains protected
Apply after 2036 for appeals job only with real authority and sufficient pay

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because the billing team could shrink before we know how appeals will work. A written cut date, paid investigation time and a real job with school-friendly hours would help. Three months of savings lets me make calls, not wait forever.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask what the customer does when a computer repeats a wrong charge in perfect language. A polite error is still money taken from someone. The appeal has to be more than another letter.

headlineQuote: A polite error is still money taken from someone.
portrait: **Omar, 43**, is a recently promoted billing-dispute manager at a large telecom company with a bachelor’s degree.
His **typical pay**, three-month reserve and some local offices help support a mortgage and two school-age children.
He uses **AI occasionally**, still asks a senior lead to check hard cases and values a real appeal route.
He stays **uneasy** in AI Plateau, becomes anxious about possible cuts and explores paid investigation work without assuming safety.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could shrink his billing team before a human appeals route exists.
whatWouldHelp: A written **cut date**, paid investigation time and a job fitting school pickup would help.
